newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had assigned its BBB plus corporate credit rating to Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile, S.A. (SQM).
S&P also assigned its BBB plus rating to SQM's $200 million (Rule 144A) loan participation certificates due 2006.

"The ratings reflect SQM's average business risk profile as the world's leading producer of specialty nitrate fertilisers and iodine, low-cost production economics, and conservative financial management," S&P said in a statement.
S&P said the rating outlook was stable.
"Conservative financial management, coupled with favourable prospects for SQM's products and development projects, bodes well for rating stability," the rating agency said.
It said Santiago, Chile based SQM is an integrated producer of natural nitrates, sulphates, iodine, and related industrial chemical products.

"The company's low cost position is derived from extensive control of high grade ores and salt brines, and efficient refining processes that extensively use solar evaporation techniques. Demand growth for the company's specialty fertiliser products (currently about two-thirds of revenues) is robust, aided by the company's expanding global distribution capabilities and technical sales staff," S&P said.
"Specialty fertilizers sell at a consistent premium to commodity fertilizers, as they improve yields of high-value crops and are better suited for certain technology-intensive settings," it said.
S&P said SQM's revenue base, currently less than $500 million, was diversified by its position as the world's leading iodine producer, controlling around 40 percent of the global market.
"In addition, a $400 million capital project will further diversify the product mix and boost profitability. Indeed it has already added a low-cost source of key raw materials," it said.
S&P said in accord with management's conservative policies, these projects were significantly prefunded through a $150 million equity offering completed in late 1995.

"Rising earnings and cash flows should cover operating needs, dividends, and a meaningful portion of larger capital projects. Thus, the financial profile is expected to remain solid, with funds from operations to total debt above 40 percent, and total debt to total capital below 35 percent," S&P said.
